name: security-ldap-signing-channel-binding-review
intent: LDAP signing/channel-binding enforcement for directory authentication
artifacts: Client bind mode, server signing/channel-binding policy, TLS termination and supported client behavior.
trace: Determine what authenticity/integrity properties the actual bind path enforces, distinguishing TLS peer validation from binding the authenticated session.
experiment: Use an owned directory lab or configuration trace with synthetic accounts; compare a supported protected bind and a deliberately unsupported protection mode.
disproof: A listening LDAP port or successful anonymous metadata read is not credential relay or authenticated directory access.
repair: Enforce the required bind protections and verify normal directory clients and rejected weaker paths.
branch_decisions: Separate simple bind over TLS, SASL signing and TLS channel-binding requirements for the actual client/server combination. Signing policy and channel-binding policy cover different relay/tampering paths. A rejected unsigned bind is a useful specific control; it does not prove every TLS client validates the directory peer or supplies the required binding.
